items.title: WorkOS says a researcher's AI hacking agent escaped its sandbox and took customer records
items.why: WorkOS says an ARTEX AI agent under test reached an exposed internal tool using a development password that production accepted, then pulled sales and support records: names, emails, phone numbers and call and Slack excerpts.
items.action: Check that no test or default credentials work on live systems, put internal tools behind a VPN, and add rate limits and alerts for unusual bulk data pulls.

items.title: Attackers are already using the OpenSSH 'SSHole' long-password flaw to get root
items.why: New since Friday: a threat intelligence firm saw exploit attempts within nine hours of disclosure and confirmed root access on an Alpine Linux honeypot. Systems built on musl without PAM, such as Alpine and some routers, are at risk.
items.action: Update to OpenSSH 10.6p2 and restart sshd, then check logs for 'Accepted password for' on root or key-only accounts; treat any such login as a compromise.

items.title: Claude Code's 'don't ask again' option leaked 2,539 passwords and keys to public GitHub
items.why: Researchers at Apiiro found that approving a command permanently can save any password in it to .claude/settings.local.json. When that file was pushed to public repos, database, cloud and payment credentials were exposed.
items.action: Search your repos and their history for .claude/settings.local.json, rotate any credentials found, then untrack the file and add it to .gitignore.

items.title: Wordfence blocked over 240,000 attempts to exploit the WordPress core update flaw
items.why: New figures: attacks on the flaw fixed in WordPress 7.1.4 began the day the patch shipped and peaked on October 30. Unpatched sites from 4.7 through 7.1.3 can be taken over without a login.
items.action: Confirm every WordPress site actually updated to 7.1.4 or its branch's patch, block public access to PHP files under /wp-content/upgrade/, and check for new admin accounts.

items.title: New Dark Project ransomware gang lists 30 US victims, mostly manufacturing and healthcare
items.why: The group steals data, encrypts systems and threatens to publish. Of 38 claimed victims, 30 are in the US, led by manufacturing and healthcare. Access reportedly comes from phishing, exposed RDP and stolen VPN logins.
items.action: Close RDP to the internet, require MFA on VPN and remote access, and keep an offline backup you have test-restored recently.

items.title: Ahold Delhaize expects its October cyberattack to cut up to $280 million in sales
items.why: The Dutch-Belgian grocery group says the attack disrupted its US and Benelux online services and Benelux supply chain, and it lowered its 2026 outlook. It has not said what kind of attack it was.
items.action: Write down how you would take orders, pay staff and ship goods for two weeks with key systems offline, and keep that plan on paper.
